column15: Core range (The Original Ten/Twelve etc.) is unpeated. Distillery also bottles peated expressions under distinct line names within the BenRiach brand itself (Curiositas, Smoky Ten/Twelve, Birnie Moss, Septendecim, Authenticus) -- captured as rules below rather than sibling brands, since they are always sold as "BenRiach <name>", not a standalone brand name. Owner Brown-Forman inferred from the 2016 GlenDronach/BenRiach/Glenglassaugh group acquisition (corroborated on the Glenglassaugh distillery page), not independently opened for BenRiach itself.

Ukrainian independent bottler based in Odesa ("Scyfion Choice"), finishes single casks from various Scottish distilleries in wine casks. Peat depends entirely on the source distillery per bottling, not on the bottler -- see distillery rows below for Dailuaine/Aultmore/Dufftown (named in this batch's samples). "Scyfion Secret Speyside" is an undisclosed-source label; left unresolved per brief guidance.
Markets itself as exclusively unpeated -- air-dried malt only, no peat smoke at any stage.

Bavarian (Schliersee) distillery; core single malt is unpeated (peated malt is only ~10% of annual barley intake). Also produces a dedicated "Bavarian PEAT" peated single malt -- captured as a rule below, not a sibling brand. Range also includes a "Bavarian RYE"; defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans malt and rye.

French independent-bottler range from La Maison du Whisky; deliberately spans every Scotch region and style, peated and unpeated, so no house peat level. Samples name Ardmore (own row in this batch), Caol Ila, Ben Nevis, Glen Elgin, Glen Ord and Linkwood -- distillery rows added below per the independent-bottler rule.

Brand identity not confidently established this pass -- no distinguishing samples beyond the bare name repeated six times. No search performed (budget spent on higher-volume brands); left unknown rather than guessed.

Japanese "World Blended Whisky" from Mars Whisky (Hombo Shuzo / Mars Shinshu distillery), released in numbered wood-finish editions (sherry cask, Mizunara, red wine, Yamazakura). Lookup attempts for this brand specifically returned no usable content this pass; peat left unknown rather than assumed.

Utah producer blending sourced whiskey (MGP and undisclosed others) with its own distillate across rye (Rendezvous Rye, Double Rye!) and bourbon (American Prairie) lines; defaultTypeName left empty since the range spans both. Full product lineup on the cited page lists no peated item and American rye/bourbon mash bills do not use peated malt, but no source explicitly states "unpeated", hence confidence=low.

12-14 ppm phenol in the malt; the distillery's own "Legacy" expression is explicitly branded "Lightly Peated", consistent with the brief's "light" band despite Ardmore's reputation as a rare peated-Highland outlier.

column15: Kind=blend per the brief's own example (no single distillery of origin disclosed). Widely known in the trade as a heavily peated Islay-style whisky from an undisclosed source distillery -- this batch's own samples include "Finlaggan Original Peaty" -- but every citation attempt this session failed (403/404, and the dedicated web search was queued exactly when the shared session search budget ran out). peatProfile is therefore left unknown rather than asserted from recall alone; a human reviewer should resolve this one specifically, it is very likely "heavy".
Own-label style blend, no independent web presence found; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch per brief long-tail default, not brand-verified.

Own-label style ("Red/Blue Edition"); country left unconfirmed -- "Glen-" prefixed names are not exclusively Scottish (cf. the EU "Glen Buchenbach" case), so origin is not assumed. Treated as an ordinary unpeated blend per brief long-tail default.
Own-label style ("McIvor Finest"), no independent web presence found; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch per brief long-tail default, not brand-verified.
Samples ("Banana", "Green Apple", "Banana Flavored") indicate a flavored whiskey/spirit-drink line rather than a conventional whisky; identity, origin and peat left unknown -- no search performed.

Established mass-market blended Scotch, popular in continental Europe. Ownership not verified this pass (attempted lookup of La Martiniquaise's brand list did not include it, so owner left empty rather than guessed); treated as unpeated per the ordinary blended-Scotch default.
Cited page confirms region/owner but does not state peat explicitly; unpeated is standard for this Speyside malt (used mainly in Ballantine's blending stock).

Recognizable budget blended Scotch; treated as unpeated per the ordinary blended-Scotch default, not independently brand-verified this pass. Input spells the roman numeral "Ii" -- preserved verbatim in alias.tsv.

Louisville, KY distillery; Core Four line (Cavehill, Heigold, Dareringer, Boxergrail) spans bourbon and a 95%-rye whiskey (Boxergrail), so defaultTypeName left empty. Official site describes mashbills with no peated malt; American whiskey mash bills do not use peat, but no source explicitly states "unpeated", hence confidence=low.

Seattle, WA American single malt distillery. Cited page does not address peat for the core range, and does not mention a "Peated" expression at all, but this batch's own samples include "Westland Peated" -- captured as a rule below from that direct evidence (sourceUrls left empty on the rule; exact intensity not independently confirmed, heavy is this session's best estimate for a dedicated peated craft release).
Triple Grain sample suggests a grain-whisky blend; country/origin not confidently identified (could be French) -- no search performed this pass.
Tomatin's peated sibling brand -- "lightly peated single malt" per the cited page, produced one week a year. Parent "tomatin" is included as its own row in this batch's producer.tsv (see below).
Single Cask sample suggests a bottler-style single-malt release rather than an ordinary blend, so the usual own-label default was not applied; origin not identified. No search performed this pass.

Sourced/blended American whiskey ("Confiscated", "The Wiseman"); current ownership not verified this pass (checked, and it is NOT listed among Sazerac Company's own brands, so owner left empty rather than guessed). defaultTypeName left empty since the wider Kentucky Owl range also includes a rye. Treated as unpeated per the American whiskey category default (bourbon/rye mash bills do not use peated malt).

Japanese Muteki sample claims Japanese origin, but true origin was not verified this pass (some "Japanese-style" whiskies are blended/bottled outside Japan); countryCode left as XX (unspecified) and peat unknown rather than assumed.

Sazerac Rye, distilled at Buffalo Trace (Frankfort, KY) per the cited page. American straight rye mash bills do not use peated malt, but the page does not explicitly address peat, hence confidence=low rather than high.
Japanese blended whisky (Matsui Whisky); lookup attempt for this brand returned no usable page content (marketing-asset page only), so peat left unknown.
Own-label style, no independent web presence found; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch per brief long-tail default, not brand-verified.
Sourced small-batch bourbon (6 Year). American bourbon mash bills do not use peated malt, but no source specific to this brand was opened, hence confidence=low.

Opened 2015 (explains the "XXI century" sample) on the old Imperial distillery site, Carron, Speyside; built mainly to supply Chivas Regal blending stock. Cited page does not state peat explicitly; unpeated is standard for this style/region.
Own-label style, no distillery by this exact name identified; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch per brief long-tail default, not brand-verified.
Sample "Fauconnier Highland's Friends" -- Fauconnier is a long-established French Scotch whisky negociant/importer; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch, not brand-verified.
Band-branded novelty whisky ("50 Heavy Metal Years"); origin not identified, no search performed this pass.
Sourced Canadian rye whiskey (Alberta Distillers stock), bottled by 35 Maple Street; not independently re-verified this pass. Canadian rye does not use peated malt.
Nashville, TN revival distillery (Nelson's Green Brier Distillery); Tennessee whiskey is a corn-based, charcoal-mellowed style unrelated to peat. Not independently re-verified this pass.
Smooth Blend sample and Irish-surname branding suggest Irish blended whiskey; ordinary Irish whiskey is unpeated (the brief's own example category). Not independently brand-verified this pass.
Tribute blend licensed by the World Federation of Robert Burns Clubs, produced by Isle of Arran Distillers; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch, not independently re-verified this pass.
Band-branded novelty whisky ("Iowa"); origin not identified, no search performed this pass.

Irish Triple Cask sample indicates Irish whiskey; ordinary Irish whiskey is unpeated (the brief's own example category). Not independently brand-verified.
